subject: Contract amendment: capacity add + model mix change (long-context model + reranker)
messages:
From: Avery Nash <avery@datasilo.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Meyer <dan@datasilo.com>, procurement@datasilo.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal + new model tests — need capacity guidance

Neha,

Quick context: our renewal with Redwood is coming up in November. Over the past quarter our product team ran a pilot of a larger long-context model for document understanding (internal name: goliath-70b-longctx) and a lightweight NN-based reranker to clean up retrieval results. Both look promising in quality tests but the inference footprint is materially higher.

We expect peak throughput to increase ~2.6x on generation traffic and a separate dedicated stream for reranker requests (QPS ~80) with low tail latency requirements. Procurement wants capacity and pricing options for a 12–18 month committed agreement that includes:
- Additional reserved GPU pool(s) sized for the new model and reranker
- Throughput guarantees (p50/p95 targets) during business hours with burst handling
- Clear model-mix fallback plan (if the large model can't be scheduled, fall back to goliath-13b or a quantized variant)

Can your team sketch options and a ballpark cost delta? We should include estimated infra lead time (any required H100 vs A100 sizing) since infra changes may take weeks.

Thanks,
Avery Nash
VP, ML Platforms — DataSilo
[Attachment: sample_error_trace.txt (text)]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Avery Nash <avery@datasilo.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal + new model tests — need capacity guidance

Avery — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the pilot quality lift. This is exactly the sort of model-mix shift that we plan for at renewal, so happy to put a concrete proposal together. High-level answers below; I attached a proposal doc and a capacity calc so you can scrutinize assumptions.

Key takeaways (high level):
- We can support goliath-70b-longctx but it materially increases GPU memory and KV-cache pressure. For consistent p95 latency under your projected traffic we recommend a dedicated pool on H100-class instances, or an A100+ quantization strategy if you'd prefer lower-cost hardware with slightly higher latency.
- For the reranker add-on, we suggest a separate reserved pool (lower GPU memory but optimized for throughput) with autoscaling capped at the committed pool size and a burst policy that borrows capacity from a shared overflow tier during high spikes.
- Term options: 12-month extension vs 18-month with stepped discounts. 18-month gives better unit pricing and higher guaranteed throughput (we can hold a slightly larger warm pool).

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom will send a technical capacity breakdown and two concrete sizing options (H100 preferred, A100 cost-optimized).
2) Marcus will outline commercials (term pricing, discount, credits for migration).
3) Grace will coordinate SOC2 evidence and procurement packet for your team.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v3.pdf; capacity_calculation_spreadsheet.xlsx

-Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal + new model tests — need capacity guidance

Hi all — dug into the numbers from the pilot logs and the perf report (attached). Short technical summary and two sizing options below. Assumptions are in the spreadsheet.

Pilot observations:
- goliath-70b-longctx (204k context) increases KV-cache size ~6–8x compared to your current goliath-13b traffic patterns. Peak token generation per-request is up ~3x.
- Reranker is small model (1–2B) but has high QPS and strict p50 latency needs (~20–30ms).

Option A (Performance-first, recommended for p95 SLOs):
- Dedicated H100 pool: 12 H100 GPUs reserved (serves model + keep warm replicas) + 4 H100 dedicated for reranker pool (shared tail capacity).
- Expected p95 latency: generation <350ms (business hours), reranker p50 <35ms.
- Risk: higher monthly commit cost; infra lead time 4–6 weeks for dedicated warm capacity.

Option B (Cost-optimized, acceptable for many clients):
- A100 80GB quantized deployment: 18 A100 GPUs reserved (larger pool due to less memory / quantization overhead) + 6 A100 for reranker.
- Expected p95 latency: generation <600ms, reranker p50 <60ms.
- Lower cost vs A but slightly higher tail latency; infra lead time 2–4 weeks.

Fallbacks and scheduling:
- We can pin a fallback policy in the control plane so that if the longctx pool is saturated requests route to goliath-13b-quantized at slightly lower quality but faster scheduling.
- Automatic reroute can be configured per-route and per-customer priority.

I've attached model_perf_report.csv and updated the capacity_calculation_spreadsheet.xlsx with the assumptions. Happy to walk through calculations on a quick call.

—Priyom Das
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model_perf_report.csv (csv)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Commercials: commit options and draft amendment language

Avery — following Priyom's sizing notes, we ran commercial models for both options. High-level commercials below; full line items are in the attached proposal PDF.

Option A (H100, performance):
- Monthly committed spend (baseline): $142,000/mo for the reserved pools described (12 H100 gen pool + 4 H100 reranker pool).
- Bursting: 20% monthly burst budget included at a premium rate (we allocate warm shared capacity for predictable bursts).
- Term: 18-month: 10% discount applied to committed pool vs 12-month. One-time migration credit of $40k if you sign within 30 days.

Option B (A100, cost-optimized):
- Monthly committed spend: $96,500/mo (18 A100 + 6 A100 reranker).
- Bursting: 15% monthly burst budget.
- Term: 12-month: standard pricing; 12-month + technical onboarding credit of $20k.

Other commercial notes:
- We will include a service appendix that codifies throughput guardrails (p50/p95 targets during business hours) and a fallback policy. SLA credits for breaches are available per the standard enterprise agreement.
- Proposed contract amendment language: add a dedicated capacity schedule, specify hardware profile, include a model-mix addendum (approved models + fallback variants), and an explicit migration window (30–60 days).

If you'd like, we can prepare an 18-month amendment with the 10% discount and the migration credit — that gets you the most predictable capacity and better unit economics.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Team — thanks for the thorough breakdown. Internal reactions: the product org prefers Option A for latency consistency; procurement favors Option B for cost but can accept Option A with the 18-month term and migration credit.

Requests before we move to signature:
- Finalized amendment doc with exact pool counts and a short-runbook for the fallback routing logic.
- Confirmation of migration timeline (we need a max 6-week migration window to coordinate infra and customer QA).
- SOC2 / compliance packet for our procurement to review (Grace, tagging you separately).

If you can get the amendment and runbook over by Friday we can route to our legal and procurement next week. We'll plan for the 18-month term and would like the migration credit included in the countersign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a call if you want to walk the docs.

—Avery
